abstract:
In spinocerebellar ataxia type 1 (SCA1), Purkinje cells fire with more variable interspike intervals before they degenerate, and reduced ion-channel expression is a proposed cause. We asked whether their channel transcript changes, applied as conductance changes, could produce this firing. We analysed public single-nucleus RNA-seq from male and female Atxn1 154Q/2Q knock-in and wild-type mice (24 discovery mice, 5-30 weeks; six held-out, 12 weeks). Knock-in Purkinje nuclei showed a reproducible transcriptional shift from 5 weeks. Transcripts of five channels, Kv3.3, BK, Kv4.3, Cav2.1 and Cav3.1, were reduced by 12 weeks (28-41 % at 18 weeks) and also lower, though not significantly for any single transcript, in ATXN1[82Q] Purkinje nuclei. We scaled the five conductances by these ratios in a published Purkinje cell model (130 parameter sets). The simulated neurons fired at 1.9 times the wild-type rate, outside the range recorded in knock-in Purkinje cells, and at 1.14 times in a second model. Scaling only Kv3.3, BK, Kv4.3 and Cav3.1, with Cav2.1 left at its wild-type value, brought both models close to the wild-type rate. With BK and Cav3.1 set from published staining, the afterhyperpolarization and depolarization-block threshold moved towards knock-in values, but by less. Dividing the five transcript ratios by the smaller knock-in membrane area (0.80 of wild type) also brought the median firing rate into the recorded range. Among versions whose median firing rate was in the recorded range, the median over parameter sets of the KI/WT ratio of the interspike-interval coefficient of variation was at most 1.57, whereas the recorded ratios of the group means were 1.8 and 2.9. In some versions, pauses in a few simulated neurons raised the ratio of the mean coefficients of variation. In these models, transcript changes alone did not reproduce the firing. Measuring spontaneous firing, Cav2.1 current density and membrane capacitance in the same knock-in and wild-type Purkinje cells, matched for age and lobule, would show whether Cav2.1 current falls less than its transcript, whether the cells are smaller, or both.

Significance StatementIn spinocerebellar ataxia type 1 (SCA1), Purkinje cells fire with more variable interspike intervals before they degenerate. Five ion-channel transcripts are lower in SCA1 knock-in Purkinje cells and, though not significantly for any single transcript, in a second SCA1 model. We asked whether these lower transcripts, taken as smaller conductances, explain the firing. In a Purkinje cell model, reducing all five conductances made the simulated neurons fire almost twice as fast as wild type, unlike knock-in Purkinje cells. Keeping Cav2.1 at its wild-type value, or correcting for the smaller knock-in membrane, brought the median firing rate close to that of knock-in cells, but the median increase in the variability of the interspike interval stayed below the recorded increase. Measuring spontaneous firing, Cav2.1 current density and membrane capacitance in the same knock-in and wild-type Purkinje cells, matched for age and lobule, would show whether Cav2.1 current falls less than its transcript, whether the cells are smaller, or both.
